chunks.title: FBR Income Tax Regulations & Slabs (Tax Year 2024-2025) — Overview & Tax Year Definitions
chunks.content:
## Overview & Tax Year Definitions
Under the Income Tax Ordinance 2001 (as amended by Finance Act 2024), Tax Year 2025 covers the period from July 1, 2024 to June 30, 2025.
An individual is classified as "Salaried" if their salary income constitutes more than 75% of their total taxable income for the year. Otherwise, they are classified as "Non-Salaried Individual / Association of Persons (AOP)".

---

## Salaried Individual Tax Slabs (Finance Act 2024)

| Slab | Taxable Income Range (PKR) | Fixed Tax (PKR) | Variable Tax Rate on Excess |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Up to 600,000 | 0 | 0% |
| 2 | 600,001 to 1,200,000 | 0 | 5% of amount exceeding PKR 600,000 |
| 3 | 1,200,001 to 2,200,000 | 30,000 | 15% of amount exceeding PKR 1,200,000 |
| 4 | 2,200,001 to 3,200,000 | 180,000 | 25% of amount exceeding PKR 2,200,000 |
| 5 | 3,200,001 to 4,100,000 | 430,000 | 30% of amount exceeding PKR 3,200,000 |
| 6 | Exceeding 4,100,000 | 700,000 | 35% of amount exceeding PKR 4,100,000 |

### High-Income Surcharge for Salaried Individuals
For individuals with taxable income exceeding PKR 10,000,000 (10 Million PKR) per annum, a surcharge of 10% on the calculated income tax liability is applied.

chunks.title: FBR Income Tax Regulations & Slabs (Tax Year 2024-2025) — Key Advance Withholding Tax (WHT) Rates (Filer vs Non-Filer)
chunks.content:
## Key Advance Withholding Tax (WHT) Rates (Filer vs Non-Filer)

| Transaction Type | Active Taxpayer (Filer) Rate | Inactive / Non-Filer Rate | Notes & Legal Threshold |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bank Cash Withdrawal | 0% | 0.6% | Applies only if daily withdrawal exceeds PKR 50,000 for non-filers |
| Bank Profits (Profit on Debt) | 15% | 30% | Deducted at source on savings accounts & fixed deposits |
| National Savings Certificates | 15% | 30% | Exemptions apply to Behbood/Pensioners accounts up to limits |
| Dividend Income (Normal) | 15% | 30% | Mutual funds & listed corporate equities |
| Motor Vehicle Purchase / Registration | 1% to 3% based on CC | 3x to 5x filer rate | Substantial punitive rates for non-filers |
| Property Purchase (Advance Tax 236K) | 3% | 10.5% (up to 15%) | Based on recorded FBR fair valuation |
| Property Sale (Advance Tax 236C) | 3% | 10% | Based on holding period and filer status |

---

chunks.title: FBR Income Tax Regulations & Slabs (Tax Year 2024-2025) — Practical Tax Planning Tips for Pakistani Earners
chunks.content:
## Practical Tax Planning Tips for Pakistani Earners
1. **Active Taxpayer List (ATL) Status**: Maintaining filer status immediately cuts withholding taxes on banking, vehicle purchases, and property transactions by 50% to 70%.
2. **Voluntary Pension System (VPS)**: Contributions to SECP-registered Voluntary Pension Schemes qualify for tax credit up to 20% of taxable income under Section 63.
3. **Medical Allowance Exemption**: Reimbursed medical expenses or cash medical allowance up to 10% of basic salary is exempt from income tax if certified by employer.

chunks.title: National Savings Organization Schemes & Profit Rates (CDNS) — Investment Limits & Eligibility Rules
chunks.content:
## Investment Limits & Eligibility Rules

### 1. Behbood Savings Certificates (BSC)
- **Minimum Investment**: PKR 5,000.
- **Maximum Limit**: PKR 7,500,000 (PKR 7.5 Million) for single individual; PKR 15,000,000 (PKR 15 Million) for joint eligible accounts.
- **Key Advantage**: Zero income tax deduction at source regardless of filer status. No compulsory Zakat deduction.

### 2. Regular Income Certificates (RIC)
- **Minimum Investment**: PKR 50,000.
- **Maximum Limit**: No upper limit for general public.
- **Premature Encashment Penalties**: Service charges apply if encashed within 1st, 2nd, 3rd, or 4th year (typically 1.0% to 0.25% of face value).

### 3. Sarwa Islamic Term Account (SITA)
- Shariah-compliant alternative to conventional certificates, structured on Mudarabah principle.
- Available in 1-year, 3-year, and 5-year tenures with monthly, half-yearly, or maturity profit disbursement.

---

chunks.title: National Savings Organization Schemes & Profit Rates (CDNS) — Tax and Advisory Guidelines for Personal Finance
chunks.content:
## Tax and Advisory Guidelines for Personal Finance
1. **Senior Family Members**: Households can optimize returns and eliminate tax drag by gifting investment capital to eligible senior family members (parents/spouses aged 60+) to utilize the BSC quota.
2. **Filer vs Non-Filer Gap**: For RIC or standard savings certificates, non-filers lose 30% of their gross earnings to withholding tax compared to 15% for filers, significantly reducing the effective net yield.

chunks.title: State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) Banking & Monetary Regulations — Overview & Monetary Policy Framework
chunks.content:
## Overview & Monetary Policy Framework
The State Bank of Pakistan regulates scheduled commercial banks, microfinance banks, and payment system operators. The Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) sets the central Policy Rate (reverse repo rate), which acts as the benchmark for commercial deposit and lending rates across the country.

---

metadata.section_title: Overview & Monetary Policy Framework
metadata.source_doc_title: State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) Banking & Monetary Regulations

chunks.title: State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) Banking & Monetary Regulations — Minimum Savings Rate Rule (SBP Floor on PLS Savings)
chunks.content:
## Minimum Savings Rate Rule (SBP Floor on PLS Savings)
Under SBP BSD Circulars, all commercial banks offering conventional Profit and Loss Sharing (PLS) savings accounts are mandated to pay a minimum profit rate linked directly to the SBP Policy Rate:
- **Floor Rule**: Commercial bank PLS savings deposit rate must be at least **Policy Rate minus 150 basis points (1.5%)**.
- **Calculation Basis**: Profit must be calculated on the **average daily balance** (or minimum monthly balance as mandated for specific legacy tiers) and credited monthly or quarterly.
- **Consumer Impact**: Savers with funds sitting in commercial savings accounts should expect returns closely tracking the current monetary cycle, avoiding negative real returns when inflation softens.

---

chunks.title: State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) Banking & Monetary Regulations — Deposit Protection Corporation (DPC) Guarantee
chunks.content:
## Deposit Protection Corporation (DPC) Guarantee
Deposits in all scheduled commercial banks are insured by the Deposit Protection Corporation (a wholly-owned subsidiary of SBP):
- **Protected Amount**: Up to **PKR 500,000 per depositor per bank**.
- **Eligible Accounts**: Current, savings, and fixed term deposits in domestic currency.
- **Strategy**: Individuals holding large cash reserves (e.g. over PKR 5M) are advised to distribute funds across multiple top-tier commercial banks to maximize systemic safety and DPC coverage.

chunks.title: Zakat & Ushr Regulations, Nisab Benchmarks & Exemption Forms — Legal Framework: Zakat and Ushr Ordinance 1980
chunks.content:
## Legal Framework: Zakat and Ushr Ordinance 1980
Under the Zakat and Ushr Ordinance 1980, compulsory deduction of Zakat is carried out annually on the 1st of Ramadan across all scheduled commercial banks and designated financial institutions on qualifying savings, PLS, and fixed deposit accounts.

---

chunks.title: Zakat & Ushr Regulations, Nisab Benchmarks & Exemption Forms — Compulsory Bank Deduction Mechanism
chunks.content:
## Compulsory Bank Deduction Mechanism

| Parameter | Regulatory Detail |
|---|---|
| **Deduction Rate** | **2.5%** flat on qualifying balances |
| **Deduction Date** | 1st of Ramadan (Valuation Date announced by Ministry of Religious Affairs) |
| **Bank Holiday** | Banks remain closed for public transactions on deduction day to process audits |
| **Accounts Subject to Deduction** | Savings Accounts, Notice Deposit Accounts, Fixed Deposit Receipts, Term Deposit Receipts (TDRs), National Savings Scheme accounts |
| **Accounts Exempt from Compulsory Deduction** | Current Accounts (Checking), Foreign Currency Accounts, Non-Muslim customer accounts, accounts with valid CZ-50 affidavit on file |

---

chunks.title: Zakat & Ushr Regulations, Nisab Benchmarks & Exemption Forms — Nisab Thresholds (Silver vs Gold)
chunks.content:
## Nisab Thresholds (Silver vs Gold)

Under Shariah and official declarations:
1. **Official State Bank Nisab (Silver Basis)**:
   - For statutory bank deductions, the Ministry of Religious Affairs calculates the Nisab based on **52.5 tolas of silver** (~612.36 grams) at the prevailing wholesale market price just prior to Ramadan.
   - Example 2024–2025 range: Approximately PKR 135,000 to PKR 150,000 depending on commodity price fluctuations. Accounts holding balances equal to or greater than this announced threshold on 1st Ramadan are subject to automatic 2.5% deduction.
2. **Wealth Calculation (Gold Basis)**:
   - Gold standard is **7.5 tolas of gold** (~87.48 grams). For personal asset wealth evaluations (cash, gold jewelry, tradable inventory), scholars generally refer to the silver threshold as the safer hurdle for compulsory duty.

---

metadata.section_title: Nisab Thresholds (Silver vs Gold)

metadata.authority: Ministry of Religious Affairs & Interfaith Harmony / SBP

chunks.title: Zakat & Ushr Regulations, Nisab Benchmarks & Exemption Forms — Zakat Exemption Procedure (Declaration Form CZ-50)
chunks.content:
## Zakat Exemption Procedure (Declaration Form CZ-50)
Individuals who belong to recognized fiqh jurisprudence that exempts them from state-level collection, or who wish to distribute their Zakat personally directly to verified beneficiaries, can seek full exemption from compulsory bank deductions:
- **Declaration Document**: **Form CZ-50** (Zakat Exemption Declaration / Affidavit on non-judicial stamp paper, attested by a Notary Public / Oath Commissioner).
- **Submission Timeline**: Must be submitted to the customer's bank branch **at least 30 days prior** to 1st of Ramadan.
- **Account Tagging**: Once recorded in the Core Banking System (CBS), the account is flagged as "Zakat Exempt", preventing any automated deduction on Ramadan 1.
